sentences.text:
1. The petitioner is before this Court seeking for the following reliefs:-
a. Issue a Writ in nature of mandamus directing the respondent authorities to pay the compensation/damages of Rs.50,00,000/- (Fifty Lakhs) for the injuries caused and disability suffered by the petitioner due to the electrocution on 04-06- 2013 for negligence in complying the statutory duties under the Electricity Act & Rules, in the interest of justice and equity.
b. Pass such other orders or directions as this Hon'ble Court deems just and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case and allow this Writ Petition, in the interest of justice.
2.
The petitioner is a permanent resident of Gunjhali Village, Sindhanur Taluk.
The petition has been filed by the victim represented by his father.

sentences.text: 3. High tension naked wires having been installed in Gunjhali Village, the villagers requested the respondent authorities to shift/removal of high tension electric naked wires, which was not acceded to.
The applications had also been submitted despite which the electric wire of 11 KV was not shifted.

4. In the meanwhile, on 04.06.2013 at about 4.30 p.m., the petitioner on seeing a pigeon sitting beside the high tension wires, passing over the house of one Tidigol Ramanna, tried to catch the pigeon and he immediately came in contract with electric high tension naked wires and due to electrocution, his right hand and left portion of the body were thrown up in the air and fell to the ground.
5. The right hand being severed at the shoulder, the petitioner was hospitalized in St.John's Hospital, Bangalore on 05.06.2013.
He was treated as an inpatient for a period of 37 days finally being discharged on 11.07.2013.

It is claimed that the petitioner incurred a sum of Rs.3,00,000/-
towards NC: 2023:KHC-K:1443 medical expenses for the said treatment.

The petitioner reported the incident of electrocution to the jurisdictional police and lodged a complaint at Turavihal police station, which came to be registered as a Crime No.139/2013 under Section 285, 338 of IPC.
It is on account of the said incident, the petitioner is before this Court claiming compensation.

6. Sri.Mahantesh Patil, learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that:
6.1. There being serious injuries which have been caused to the petitioner resulting in life long disability.

The petitioner has lost 80% of sensation in the left hand fingers and his right hand has been amputated at the shoulder level, which would have an impact on his future life and as such, it is submitted that on account of the said injuries, a legal notice had been issued on 23.09.2013 vide Annexure-G to the respondents claiming compensation amounts.
The same being replied to in the reply notice dated 26.09.2013 denying the compensation, the petitioner is before this Court seeking compensation.

6.2. By relying on a judgment of Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Rekha and others vs.
Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Limited and others1, he submits that it is not required for the petitioner to approach the Civil Court.

sentences.text: This Court has the adequate and more powers to exercise on such situation and to award compensation and quantifying the same in terms of methodology resorted to so that computation as done under Motor Vehicles Accident Cases.
He submits that the occurrence of the events not being in dispute, the respondent authorities are required to make necessary compensation.

Sri.Ravindra Reddy, learned counsel for the respondents would submit that:

there are disputed question of facts requiring trial and as such, the above matter cannot be adjudicated by this Court and the petitioner being required to be relegated to the Civil Court.

7.2. Secondly, he submits that in order to claim compensation, the petitioner has to establish negligence on part of the respondent - authorities and no such negligence having been established, no claim could be made against the respondent - authorities by the petitioner.

7.3. Lastly, he submits that the petitioner and his family members having constructed the house below the existing line, they were asked to vacate the premises, which was not so done and as such, the respondent authorities cannot be held liable to make payment of compensation due to the petitioner and his NC: 2023:KHC-K:1443 family member having put up construction below the high-tension wire.
On these grounds, he submits that the above petition would require to be dismissed.

8. Heard Sri.Mahantesh Patil, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.Ravindra Reddy, learned counsel for the respondents No.1 to 3 and perused the papers.
9.

The submission of Sri.Ravindra Reddy, learned counsel for the respondents No.1 to 3 firstly is that there are disputed questions of fact and as such, the petitioner would have to be relegated to the Civil Court.
No written objections have been filed in the present proceedings.
Except for the oral submission, which have been made, there is nothing on record to indicate any disputed question of facts.
Be that as it may.
The occurrence of the incident is not in dispute.
The injuries which have been caused to the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1443 petitioner is also not in dispute.
The cause of injuries being the naked electric high-tension wire is also not in dispute.
What is only in dispute is that the respondent - authorities claiming that they are not liable to make payment of compensation.
This in my considered opinion cannot be a dispute requiring relegation of petitioner to the Civil Court as contended or otherwise.

10. A perusal of Annexure-G1 being the reply notice which had been issued clearly and categorically indicates that respondent - authorities had called upon the petitioner and his family members to vacate the premises.

This by itself would establish that the existence of the electrical high-tension wire above the house of the petitioner and/or his neighbour was so dangerous that the officer of the respondent had called upon the petitioner and his family to vacate the premises.

This fact would be sufficient to establish that the accident caused NC: 2023:KHC-K:1443 resulting in injuries to the petitioner was not so remote but was proximate to the existence of the high-tension wires.

11. The second contention of Sri.Ravindra Reddy, learned counsel for the respondents is that there was a notice which had been issued calling upon the petitioner and his family members to vacate the premises and they not having done so cannot claim damages.
Though in the reply notice, there is a contention raised that notice had been issued prior to the incident, no copy of the said notice has been produced.

As observed above, the fact that such a notice had been issued would indicating that even according to the respondents, possibility of grievous injuries being caused to the residents was under Yankanagouda S/O Hanumangouda vs The Managing Director And Ors on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175565322/
4 contemplation.

sentences.text: If that be so, it was for the respondents to have taken adequate steps to vacate any person residing under high-tension wire, if the same was so permissible under law.
Not having - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1443 done so, the respondents cannot now contend that they are not liable to make payment of compensation.

12. Insofar as the writ remedy is concerned, a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court as observed above in Rekha's case supra has come to a categorical conclusion that these kinds of matters can be considered, and compensation can be awarded.
In that view of the matter, the said submission is also rejected.

13. Now coming to the quantification of compensation, the petitioner was 10 years old as on the date of the incident and the disability as certified by the treating doctor is stated to be 90% of the disability of the whole body.
The said certification has been issued by St.John Medical College and Hospital, Bangalore on 21.09.2013.

entities.text: St.John Medical College and Hospital, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The history of the accident as per said certificate is that the accident is on account of - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1443 high-tension electric wire and burns to the right upper limb.
The disability is stated to be permanent right shoulder disarticulation.

The photographs produced along with the petition indicates that the right arm of the petitioner has been amputated at the shoulder level and on the left side of the body, there are severe burn injuries.
The disability having been quantified at 90%, there is no particular objection filed in that regard to the disability certificate by the respondents.
14. The petitioner claims that they made payment of Rs.3,00,000/- as medical expenses at the hospital.
However, no bills have been produced in this regard by the petitioner.
Hence, the awardal of compensation on account of treatment and hospitalization cannot be considered.

15. Insofar as loss of earning is concerned, the petitioner having suffered permanent disability of 90% with - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1443 amputation of the right arm at the shoulder level, the loss of earning can be determined by taking into consideration the notional income for the year 2013, when the accident occurred, being Rs.7,000/- and in terms of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier would be '18'.
Hence, the compensation liable to be paid on this account would be Rs.7,000 x 12 x 18 x 90% = Rs.13,60,800/-.

Considering that the petitioner had been hospitalization for a period of 37 days, I am of the considered opinion that attendant charges at the rate of Rs.2,000/- per day could be awarded,
which would come to Rs.74,000/-, rounded off to Rs.75,000/-.

17. Considering the nature of injuries, which have been caused, the right arm being amputated at the shoulder level, which would also resulted in disfigurement, I am of the considered opinion that - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1443 compensation towards pain and suffering would be awarded at Rs.5,00,000/-.

18. The marriage prospects of the petitioner being adversely affected, an amount of Rs.3,00,000/-
has been awarded on this account.

19. The petitioner has produced an estimation of Aston Healthcare towards right shoulder disarticulation cosmetic prostheses with acrylic socket mechanical shoulder joint, elbow joint,
cosmetic glove myoelectric 1 degree system harness system, I am of the considered opinion that the said estimation is reasonable and as such, would have to be awarded.
Hence, it is deemed to award Rs.4,00,000/- towards future medical expenses.
Hence, the total compensation thereof is as under:-

In that view of the matter, I pass the following:
ORDER i.
The Writ Petition is allowed.
ii. A mandamus is issued directing the respondents - authorities to make payment of a sum of Rs.26,35,800/- along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of the accident till the realization.
The same shall be realized within a period of 6 weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order, failing which the interest payable shall stand enhanced to 9% per annum.
